question_stem:
A varying current $I$ passes through a resistor of resistance $R$ in the circuit shown in Fig. 7.1.
{{figure:9702_w23_43_q07_figure_7_1}}
Fig. 7.1
Fig. 7.2 shows the variation with time $t$ of $I$.
{{figure:9702_w23_43_q07_figure_7_2}}
Fig. 7.2
The current has magnitude $2I_0$ when it is in the positive direction and $I_0$ when it is in the negative direction. The period of the variation of the current is $T$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: Determine expressions, in terms of $I_0$ and $R$, for the power $P$ dissipated in the resistor for the times when:
parts.text: the current is in the negative direction

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the current is in the positive direction.

parts.label: (b)
(c)(i)
parts.part_stem: Use your answer in (b) to determine an expression, in terms of $I_0$ and $R$, for:
parts.text: the mean power $\langle P \rangle$ in the resistor

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) current $I_{\text{r.m.s.}}$ in the resistor.
